summary: Backend-only verification of the application.yml fix that removes the hardcoded `hibernate.default_schema: public` in ebms-orchestrator, replacing it with a Spring placeholder `${SPRING_JPA_DEFAULT_SCHEMA:}` (empty default). Verified: (1) mvn compile of ebms-common+ebms-orchestrator SUCCESS. (2) YAML parses via Spring's YamlPropertiesFactoryBean (SnakeYAML). (3) A new JUnit test `ApplicationYamlSchemaPropertyTest` (4 tests, ALL PASS) asserts: raw YAML value equals the placeholder literal (no hardcoded 'public'); resolves to empty string when env var unset; resolves to override value when set. (4) Hibernate 6.6.4.Final bytecode-level analysis confirms an empty-string `hibernate.default_schema` is safely equivalent to unset (Identifier.toIdentifier returns null on empty via StringHelper.isEmpty guard) → NO malformed '.tablename' SQL possible; SQL will be unqualified and driven purely by the JDBC connection's search_path. (5) Repo-wide grep confirms no other hardcoded schema references remain outside the now-parameterized line.

critical_code_review_comments: Fix is correct and generic. `default_schema: ${SPRING_JPA_DEFAULT_SCHEMA:}` uses Spring's placeholder syntax with empty default. HAVEN k3s deployment can override via env var if ever needed, but by default the JDBC url's `currentSchema=orchestrator` search_path parameter is authoritative.

SAFETY of empty string proven via Hibernate 6.6.4.Final bytecode (hibernate-core-6.6.4.Final.jar → org.hibernate.boot.model.naming.Identifier.toIdentifier(String,boolean,boolean)): first instruction is `StringHelper.isEmpty(input); ifeq → aconst_null; areturn`. An empty or null input yields a null Identifier, which in SqlStringGenerationContextImpl becomes a null `defaultSchema` field. `schemaWithDefault(null)` then returns the entity-declared schema (which is also null since @Table has no schema attribute), so the qualified name emits WITHOUT any schema prefix — Postgres then uses the connection's search_path. No risk of malformed '.ebms_message' identifier.

Spring Boot 3.4 note: an empty-string placeholder value IS passed through to Hibernate's property map as the empty string "" (not stripped), which is what the empty-check in Identifier.toIdentifier handles. Verified indirectly via the property-resolution test — the value resolves to "" (not null), and Hibernate handles both cases identically.

Regression grep clean: only the parameterized `default_schema: ${SPRING_JPA_DEFAULT_SCHEMA:}` line remains in orchestrator/cpa/crypto. EbmsMessageEntity's @Table has no schema attribute (already generic, unchanged as noted). cpa-service and crypto-service have no default_schema override at all.

Optional hardening (not required): consider adding a startup log line reporting the effective schema resolution — e.g., log `spring.jpa.properties.hibernate.default_schema` value at INFO on boot — this would make on-call diagnostics of any future 'wrong schema' incident trivial.

rca of the issue.bug: Two Postgres schemas (public.ebms_message with 2 stale PROCESSING rows, orchestrator.ebms_message with 4 correct DELIVERED rows) diverged because Hibernate was writing to `public` while Flyway followed the connection's search_path (`orchestrator`).
rca of the issue.root_cause: ebms-orchestrator/src/main/resources/application.yml previously hardcoded `spring.jpa.properties.hibernate.default_schema: public`. In Hibernate 6.x, an explicit default_schema value is baked into SqlStringGenerationContextImpl.defaultSchema (via Identifier.toIdentifier), which then prefixes EVERY generated CRUD/select SQL with `public.` — overriding whatever the JDBC connection's `currentSchema=orchestrator` parameter would otherwise imply through PG's search_path.
rca of the issue.fix_verification: Line changed to `default_schema: ${SPRING_JPA_DEFAULT_SCHEMA:}`. When the env var is unset (the production case), the value resolves to an empty string, which Hibernate's Identifier.toIdentifier() treats as null (verified via bytecode of StringHelper.isEmpty guard). Result: `defaultSchema` field is null → no schema prefix in generated SQL → Postgres resolves table names via search_path → writes land in `orchestrator.ebms_message` matching Flyway migrations. If a deployment ever needs an explicit override (e.g., multi-tenant), setting SPRING_JPA_DEFAULT_SCHEMA restores explicit behaviour — proven by the 4th unit test.
